title: GNN+PPO for Dynamic Flexible Job-Shop Scheduling under Stochastic Perturbations: reproducibility package
description:
Code, trained checkpoints, experimental results (E0–E8), statistical analysis pipeline, and camera-ready figures for a master's thesis evaluating a heterogeneous GNN+PPO policy on flexible job-shop scheduling (JSSP/FJSP).

Five pre-registered hypotheses (frozen before any result existed — see thesis/PreRegistration.md) were tested: H1 (static competitiveness vs. priority dispatching rules / CP-SAT / GA), H2 (size generalization, zero-shot), H3 (robustness under breakdowns / stochastic processing times / dynamic arrivals), H4 (a disruption-aware reward term, κ ∈ {0.5, 1.0}), and H5 (decision latency vs. CP-SAT). Four hypotheses were rejected and one accepted; every result — including the four rejections — is diagnosed to a concrete, reported mechanism (e.g. H4's rejection traces to a training-regime effect quantified in the report, not left as an unexplained negative result).

This deposit is the complete, long-term reproduction artifact: it includes the trained model checkpoints the accompanying git repository deliberately excludes (regenerable, but large) so that E1–E8 can be reproduced without retraining. See README.md for exact commands, expected runtime/hardware per experiment, and a quick smoke-test procedure.
